record.paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
record.original_question: For empirical risk minimization in operator learning under statistical noise, Theorem 1 gives a nonparametric rate that is at best n^{-1/2}. Is this rate merely an artifact of the proof technique used in the statistical-learning analysis, or does it reflect a genuine minimax barrier for the noisy operator-learning problem?

evidence.quote: A remaining question is whether the nonparametric rate in Thm. 1 (which is at best n−1/2) is an artifact of the statistical learning analysis in the noisy setting, or a genuine minimax barrier.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be separable Hilbert spaces, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a class of (e.g., Lipschitz or higher-regularity) operators $F:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$. Suppose we observe i.i.d. noisy input–output pairs
$$ (X_i, Y_i)_{i=1}^n, \qquad Y_i = F^\star(X_i) + \xi_i, $$
where $F^\star\in\mathcal{F}$ is the unknown target operator, $X_i$ is drawn from some probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{X}$, and $\xi_i$ is centered noise on $\mathcal{Y}$ (e.g., Gaussian with bounded covariance) independent of $X_i$. For an estimator $\widehat{F}_n$ depending only on the data, define the squared $L^2(\mu)$-risk
$$ \mathcal{R}(\widehat{F}_n, F^\star) = \mathbb{E}\,\|\widehat{F}_n - F^\star\|_{L^2(\mu;\mathcal{Y})}^2. $$
Standard statistical-learning analyses of empirical risk minimization over $\mathcal{F}$ produce upper bounds on $\sup_{F^\star\in\mathcal{F}} \mathcal{R}(\widehat{F}_n, F^\star)$ that decay no faster than $n^{-1/2}$, even when the complexity of $\mathcal{F}$ would otherwise allow a faster nonparametric rate in the noiseless setting.

Question: Determine whether the rate $n^{-1/2}$ is a genuine minimax barrier for noisy operator learning, i.e., whether
$$ \inf_{\widehat{F}_n}\;\sup_{F^\star\in\mathcal{F}}\;\mathcal{R}(\widehat{F}_n, F^\star) \;\gtrsim\; n^{-1/2} $$
holds for natural infinite-dimensional regularity classes $\mathcal{F}$, or whether this $n^{-1/2}$ ceiling is merely an artifact of the proof technique used in the statistical-learning upper-bound analysis and can be improved by a different estimator or analysis.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (arXiv:2512.17805, "Towards Sharp Minimax Risk Bounds for Operator Learning") makes substantial progress: it establishes a curse of sample complexity for Lipschitz/Hölder operator classes, showing that for generic finite-regularity operator classes the minimax risk cannot decay at algebraic rates, while for more restrictive holomorphic classes ERM achieves rates faster than $n^{-1/2}$ such as $n^{-(1/p - 1/2)}$. This indicates that the $n^{-1/2}$ wall is not universal but depends sharply on the class; a complete resolution of whether $n^{-1/2}$ is a genuine minimax floor in all natural noisy settings has not been fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Towards Sharp Minimax Risk Bounds for Operator Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes minimax risk bounds for operator learning, showing curse of sample complexity for Lipschitz/Hölder classes and faster-than-Monte-Carlo rates for holomorphic classes via ERM.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial resolution: $n^{-1/2}$ can be both attained as a minimax floor in some regimes and surpassed in stronger-regularity (holomorphic) regimes.

status_evidence.title: A short tour of operator learning theory
status_evidence.snippet: States the question of whether the $n^{-1/2}$ nonparametric rate is an artifact of statistical learning analysis or a genuine minimax barrier as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as open in the survey.
